groups.label: Gene's Family
groups.blurb: The Lankfords of Lincoln County, Kentucky.

groups.label: Navy Shipmates & Officers
groups.blurb: U.S.S. New Orleans (CA-32), F Division, and beyond.

groups.label: Others Mentioned
groups.blurb: People named in the letters whose circle is unclear.

people.name: Raymond Eugene "Gene" Lankford
people.bio: The young sailor who wrote essentially all of these letters; born 1921 in Stanford, Lincoln County, Kentucky. He served aboard the U.S.S. New Orleans (CA-32) in the F Division, courting Joan Northcutt by mail throughout the war.
people.note: Son of William Porter Lankford and Marguerite Lynn Lankford, of Stanford, Lincoln County, Kentucky.

photo.alt: A young sailor in dress whites sits on the grass beneath a tree in Honolulu.
photo.caption: Honolulu, before the war.

people.name: Joan Northcutt Lankford
people.bio: The Stanford, Kentucky girl Gene courted by mail and married on April 20, 1943. Her maiden name was Northcutt; she lived on Route 1, Stanford, and is the recipient of nearly all the letters.
people.note: Maiden name Northcutt. Daughter of Joe E. Northcutt (1887-1932) and Anna Green Wood (1898-1988); married Gene 20 Apr 1943. Joan's family confirmed via WikiTree (Northcutt-199).

people.name: Marguerite Lynn Lankford
people.bio: Gene's mother, who does most of the family's letter-writing. She frequently worries about Gene being in the Navy, writes about home life being lonesome, and at one point asks about troubles between Gene and Joan.

people.name: William Porter Lankford
people.bio: Gene's father, who rarely writes (Mother does most of the writing). He keeps Gene updated on home news such as tobacco prices, his old Ford, and family illnesses, and is described by Gene as always cracking jokes.

people.name: Carroll Lankford
people.bio: Gene's older brother, who had served in the Navy for about four years before Gene enlisted. He repeatedly gets out of and called back into the Navy, works in Detroit, has an operation, and his relationship with Louise Dunagan sours over the course of the letters.
people.note: Confirmed brother; had served in the Navy before Gene. Confirmed via Gene's 2008 Somerset obituary (Find A Grave #27110511).

people.name: Thomas "Tom" Lankford
people.bio: Gene's brother, called Tom, Thomas, or Tommy. He worked in Detroit with Carroll, was later drafted/enlisted into the Army, and was stationed at Tacoma, Washington. Whether 'Tom'/'Tommy' always refers to this same brother is sometimes ambiguous in the text.
people.note: Confirmed brother (Thomas Lankford). Confirmed via Gene's 2008 Somerset obituary (Find A Grave #27110511).

people.name: Martha Lankford Broaddus
people.bio: Gene's sister, who trained and worked as a nurse, had her appendix out, and married. She corresponded with both Gene and Joan.
people.note: Confirmed sister; married name Broaddus. Confirmed via Gene's 2008 Somerset obituary (Find A Grave #27110511).

people.name: James Edward "Jim" Lankford
people.bio: Gene's brother James Edward, called Jim; the youngest of the Lankford brothers, fond of his goats. He survived Gene and was living in Danville, Kentucky, in 2008.
people.note: Confirmed brother James Edward Lankford of Danville, KY. Confirmed via Gene's 2008 Somerset obituary (Find A Grave #27110511).

people.name: Earl
people.bio: Gene's brother, who attended Highland school and later worked in Detroit with their brother Carroll as he neared draft age.
people.note: Confirmed brother (Earl Lankford), not a cousin. Confirmed via Gene's 2008 Somerset obituary (Find A Grave #27110511).

people.name: Ann
people.bio: A relative connected to Gene's family ('Momma was looking for Anne down'). Possibly Gene's sister Ann, though one mention (L29, commenting on Joan's hair) could be a person in Joan's circle.
people.note: Not listed among Gene's siblings in the 2008 obituary (his sisters were Martha and Alberta), so 'Ann' is likely a niece, in-law, or someone in Joan's circle.

people.name: Alberta Lankford Brady
people.bio: Gene's sister, who corresponded with him; Gene and Joan once made a trip to see her. She married into the Brady family.
people.note: Confirmed sister; married name Brady. Confirmed via Gene's 2008 Somerset obituary (Find A Grave #27110511).

people.name: Bill
people.relation: Gene's relative or family friend (paired with Alberta)
people.bio: A man paired with Alberta who wrote Gene a warm letter telling him to hurry back and marry his sweetheart. Likely Alberta's husband; relation to Gene unclear.
people.note: Paired with Alberta in the letters; possibly her husband (Alberta married a Brady). Distinct from Joan's uncle Bill and the 'Bill' who had the flu.

people.name: Louise Dunagan
people.bio: A woman from Stanford, Kentucky (Route 4) involved with Gene's brother Carroll; she was glad to see Carroll home but their relationship sours, and she later goes with another man from Michigan. She corresponds warmly with Gene and travels (Ohio, New Orleans).
people.note: Marriage vs courtship with Carroll not fully clear; the bare 'Louise' in L92 and L107 merged here.

people.name: Peggy Northcutt
people.bio: A young girl in Joan's household, identified in a Christmas card as Joan's sister Peggy Northcutt. She is in school, loves her cats, and Gene regularly sends his regards to her. A few 'Peggy' mentions are loosely grouped with Gene's family in the raw extraction but most clearly point to Joan's sister.
people.note: Joan's sister (named on the L73 Christmas card). Joan's siblings on WikiTree are Frances W. Northcutt (b.1929) and a private sister; 'Peggy' is likely one of them, exact match not yet confirmed.

people.name: Anna Green Wood (Northcutt)
people.bio: Joan's mother, Anna Green Wood (1898-1988), of Lincoln County, Kentucky; widow of Joe E. Northcutt. Gene speaks warmly of her and believed she knew he was in love with Joan.
people.note: Identified as Anna Green Wood. Joan's family confirmed via WikiTree (Northcutt-199).

people.name: Joan's grandmother
people.bio: Joan's grandmother, who at one point was 'mad' at Gene over some trouble he and Joan caused but later forgave them. She grows increasingly ill over the late letters and eventually dies, with Gene offering his condolences.
people.note: Joan's grandmother, on the Wood or Northcutt side; she grew ill and died during the war. Specific identity not yet confirmed.

people.name: Uncle Bill
people.bio: Joan's uncle, mentioned by Gene as likely to be listening to something over the radio.
people.note: Distinct from the 'Bill' paired with Alberta and the 'Bill' who had the flu.

people.name: Bill (Joan's circle)
people.relation: Someone in Joan's circle who was ill
people.bio: A person Joan mentioned who had the flu twice; Gene sympathizes. Relation to Joan unclear, and may overlap with another 'Bill' in the letters.
people.note: Possibly the same as Joan's uncle Bill or the Alberta-paired Bill; kept separate due to different context.

people.name: Buster
people.relation: A boy in Joan's/Gene's hometown circle
people.bio: A boy mentioned alongside Peggy and Jim who keeps goats; once written up humorously over '13 kisses.' He writes Gene a letter at one point. His exact circle (Joan's or Gene's family) is unclear.
people.note: Group ambiguous between joan-circle and gene-family.

people.name: Charlotte
people.bio: A friend of Joan's who named her baby brother after Gene and went horseback riding with Joan up to Sugar Loaf Mountain. Spelled both 'Charolette' and 'Charlotte.'
people.note: Two spellings merged as one person.

people.name: Elizabeth McKinney
people.bio: A friend of Joan's who spends weekends with her. Referred to by full name once and just 'Elizabeth' later.

people.name: Mr. Hampton
people.relation: An older man from Stanford whom Gene had met
people.bio: An older, well-regarded man from Stanford, Kentucky, whom Gene met getting off the train. He falls ill with pneumonia and is later reported dead, which surprises Gene.

people.name: Mrs. Holyclaw
people.bio: A local acquaintance who went to Arizona for her health, mentioned in passing.
people.note: OCR/surname spelling uncertain.

people.name: Mr. Mc.—
people.relation: Person involved in trouble at Highland (likely teacher/coach)
people.bio: A man, likely a teacher or coach, tied to 'the trouble the girls had at Highland'; Gene speculates the boys had reason to get even with him. Identity unclear.
people.note: Surname truncated in the source.

people.name: Jack "Johnny" Parkhurst
people.relation: Gene's Navy shipmate and closest friend (U.S.S. New Orleans, F Division, radar operator)
people.bio: Gene's closest Navy friend aboard the U.S.S. New Orleans, a radar operator in the F Division who worked in the office. The two were constant companions on liberty, requested transfers together, and Jack (called 'Johnny' by his wife) married Mary Louise Pendleton on December 25 and was later transferred off the ship.
people.note: 'Johnny' confirmed as Jack's nickname by his wife's letter (L102).

people.name: Mary Louise Parkhurst
people.relation: Wife of Gene's shipmate Jack "Johnny" Parkhurst
people.bio: Jack Parkhurst's bride (nee Mary Louise Pendleton), whom Jack married on December 25. She writes Gene a friendly letter (L102), noting Gene's picture appears in Johnny's Hawaii album and that he was the best radar operator on the ship.
people.note: Maiden name Pendleton; married name Parkhurst.

people.name: Donald V. "Don" Chapin
people.relation: Gene's Navy shipmate and best friend (coxswain; later U.S.S. Rowe)
people.bio: A coxswain and one of Gene's best friends aboard the New Orleans, who married a girl in Seattle and worried about the wife (Betty) he left behind. He was later transferred to the U.S.S. Rowe and wrote Gene a letter (L101) about a misunderstanding over a note Gene sent Betty.

people.name: Betty Chapin
people.relation: Wife of Gene's shipmate Don Chapin
aliases: the wife he left in Seattle
people.bio: Don Chapin's wife, whom Gene counted as a friend. A letter Gene sent her upset her, prompting Don's letter (L101). Don worried about her while at sea.
people.note: 'the wife he left in Seattle' (L71) inferred to be Betty.

people.name: Officer Riley
people.bio: The division officer aboard Johnny Parkhurst's ship, quoted (via Mrs. Parkhurst's letter) as saying Johnny was the best radar operator on the ship.

people.name: Yankoul
people.relation: A Marine aboard the U.S.S. New Orleans
people.bio: A Marine from Texas aboard the U.S.S. New Orleans who was always getting the men's mail posted. Surname reading is uncertain.
people.note: OCR/name reading uncertain.

people.name: The Tellner boy
people.relation: Navy buddy whom Joan spoke to by phone
people.bio: A Navy buddy of Gene's whom Joan once spoke to over the phone; they toured Los Angeles, San Pedro, and nearby towns before Gene left Long Beach. Surname reading is uncertain.
people.note: Surname reading uncertain.

people.name: Maudsley
people.bio: A Navy man mentioned by Don Chapin in his letter to Gene; context and relation unclear.
people.note: Identity/relation unclear.

people.name: J.B. Davidson
people.bio: An old pal of Gene's from Stanford who moved back to town and later served abroad in England. Gene wrote him letters and at one point asked Joan to find his address. Initials appear as both J.B. and J.D.
people.note: J.B./J.D. spelling merged as one person.

people.name: Jeannie
people.bio: A friend or acquaintance of Gene's who teaches school at McKinney and writes to him. Relation unclear.
people.note: Relation unclear.

people.name: Billie Tilds
people.bio: An acquaintance Gene mentions he could easily 'look up.' Relation and surname reading unclear.
people.note: Relation and surname uncertain.

people.name: Mrs. Gentry
people.bio: A well-liked woman from back home who had died; Gene laments that her family will have a hard time without her.

people.name: Joan (child/relative, not the recipient)
people.relation: A different person named Joan in the home circle
people.bio: A second person named Joan, distinct from the recipient, who got sick on cherry preserves; possibly a child or relative in the home circle.
people.note: Distinct from recipient Joan; identity unclear.

people.name: Carl
people.bio: A person whose being home surprised Gene; likely a relative or acquaintance. Could be an OCR variant but appears alongside a separate 'Carroll' mention in the same letter, so kept distinct.
people.note: Gene's brothers per the 2008 obituary were Thomas, Lewis Zane, William and Robert (infant twins), Carroll, Earl, and James Edward; 'Carl' matches none directly and remains unidentified.

people.name: Nancy Whitt
people.relation: Sender of a Christmas card to Joan and Peggy
people.bio: Signed a Christmas card sent to Joan and her sister Peggy; a family or friend correspondent. Surname reading uncertain.
people.note: Surname reading uncertain.

people.name: Mr. Daly
people.bio: Mentioned once in a passage with uncertain OCR; identity and relation unclear.
people.note: OCR reading and identity uncertain.

people.name: John
people.relation: Unclear (possibly an affectionate address or OCR misreading)
people.bio: A 'John' appearing in one line that may be an affectionate address to Joan or an OCR misreading rather than a real third party.
people.note: May not be a real person; possible OCR/address artifact.

people.name: Gene's aunts
people.bio: Gene's aunts, referenced collectively as knowing he is in love with Joan. Specific but unnamed.
people.note: Collective, unnamed reference.

people.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
people.bio: President Franklin D. Roosevelt, mentioned by Gene in connection with the election and his pledge not to send American boys to Europe.

people.name: Adolf Hitler
people.bio: Adolf Hitler, referenced by Gene both in joking comparisons and bitterly as 'that fool in Germany' responsible for the war.
people.note: 'that fool in Germany' (L50) inferred to be Hitler.

people.name: Benito Mussolini
people.bio: Benito Mussolini, referenced alongside Hitler in a joking comparison.

people.name: Walter Pidgeon
people.bio: Actor in the film 'Manhunt,' which Gene mentions seeing.

people.name: Joan Bennett
people.bio: Actress in the film 'Manhunt,' which Gene mentions seeing.

people.name: Mary Martin
people.bio: Actress in 'Kiss The Boys Goodbye,' a film Gene mentions seeing.

people.name: Don Ameche
people.bio: Actor in 'Kiss The Boys Goodbye,' a film Gene mentions seeing.

people.name: Lana Turner
people.bio: Movie star whom one of Gene's shipmates went down to see.

people.name: Chaplain Howell Forgy
people.bio: The Navy chaplain Howell Forgy, who wrote a book about the U.S.S. New Orleans (famous for 'Praise the Lord and pass the ammunition'), referenced in Mrs. Parkhurst's letter to Gene.
people.note: Spelled 'Chaplin Forgy' in the source.

people.name: Tyrone Power
people.bio: Actor in "Blood & Sand," a film Gene saw and recommended to Joan.
people.note: Caught by the completeness pass; missed in the first extraction.
